responses.text: The camera window's levels are now set automatically, using the 25th to 99.99th percentile of the frame. The range is 900 to 1600 counts. This only changes the display; the instrument itself is untouched.

I ran Auto L/R illumination on the three acquisition rows, so each tile's light sheet is now chosen by its X position relative to the median X. Row a.tif (x = 0) is set to Right, and rows b.tif (x = 1000) and c.tif (x = 2000) are set to Left. The list is otherwise unchanged and nothing has been started.
I'll take a snap first, then run the focus optimizer over ±100 µm without accepting the result, so focus stays where it is.
The optimizer is waiting for a decision, so I'll discard its result. That keeps focus where it is and clears the pending step.

I took a snap, which was saved to `D:\claude-scratch\pr8\tmp\mesospim_snap_f1v5ksee\remote_20260917-120000.tif`. Then I ran the focus optimizer over ±100 µm around f = 1000.

The sharpness peaked at the current position (f = 1000), so the optimizer found no better focus. I discarded its result, so focus stays at f = 1000 and nothing moved. The shutter was closed during the snap and the optimizer, so the snap may not show a usable image; I haven't checked the picture.
The tile overview window is closed. The other windows (main, camera, acquisition manager) are still open, and the microscope itself was not touched.
The camera window's colour map is now magma. The levels are unchanged at 100 to 3000 counts, and I haven't touched the instrument.

Both stacks give the same depth of field, but the tilted one shows sag and the flat one doesn't.

- **Depth of field:** 28.5 µm for both.
- **Sag:** flat is 0 µm in x and y. Tilted is 5.8 µm in x, 0 µm in y, and 3.1 µm on average.
- **Best plane:** both peak at z index 10 (100 µm), with the same mean contrast at best focus (0.4).

The analysis used the tool's defaults: a 10 µm z step, and no magnification or pixel pitch given. The depth and sag values are only as good as those defaults, so if your stacks used a different z step, tell me and I'll rerun it. I did not move the stage or change any settings.

The galvos are frozen for alignment: I turned on the Freeze galvo toggle, which sets their amplitude to 0. The ETL amplitudes and the other settings are unchanged. To resume scanning, turn the toggle off, and I'll do that when you ask.
I'll read the current acquisition list first, to see which laser each row uses.

Both rows in the acquisition list (a.tif and b.tif) already use the 488 nm laser, so they form a single group and I didn't need to reorder anything. I've set the acquisition table to group by laser, which is a display setting only; the rows and their order are unchanged. If you later add rows on another laser, tell me and I'll arrange them so each laser's rows sit together.
The camera window levels are now set to 200 to 3000. The display histogram runs 0 to 4000, and the window shows the whole frame. This changes only the display, not the instrument.

The line ROI runs from (100, 100) to (400, 500) and is 500 pixels long. The camera window reports that as 500 µm, but that assumes 1.0 µm per pixel. The instrument's camera pixel size reads null, so 1.0 µm looks like a default rather than a calibrated value. Treat 500 µm as provisional until the pixel size is calibrated at the current 1x zoom. I haven't changed anything on the instrument; the line overlay is now shown in the camera window.
The camera window's colour map is now viridis. The levels are still at 100–3000 counts.

The camera window now uses a custom green lookup table: black for the darkest pixels, through to full green for the brightest. The display levels are still 100 to 3000 counts, so the gradient spans that range. I only changed the display; the instrument itself was not touched.
The left laser's maximum amplitude is now set to 80% of its maximum. The change was accepted and the operation completed. I didn't change any other laser timing settings.
The contrast map window is now open. It shows the colormap (jet) with levels 0 to 1 and the default 8×8 map grid. The camera window is also open, showing the 2048×2048 frame.
The stack has 3 frames (indices 0–2), so the final frame is index 2.
The beads stack is open in the camera window, and it is now on its final frame, index 2 (the stack has 3 frames, 512 × 512 px). I didn't move the stage or change any instrument settings.

I couldn't get a usable screenshot of the tile overview. Both requests were applied, but the returned image is a 1×1 blank PNG, so there is nothing to show you.

The window itself is open and reports "Status: OK". Its scale is 0.01 and it is scrolled to the centre (0.5, 0.5). If you can see the window on screen, it should be fine. If you want, I can try saving the picture to a file instead, or open the camera window so you can check the view.

The processor chain now has a single GaussianBlur step with sigma 2.0 pixels, and the chain is enabled. It applies to the live view and to saved images. I haven't saved the chain to file. I haven't taken a frame to check the effect yet; say if you want one.
I'll check the file exists and look up the optics info the analysis needs for pixel size.

The file is there. The optics info gives 1.0 µm per pixel at 1x, which is the current zoom, but I don't know which zoom or z-step the stack was taken with. I'll run the analysis on the 1x pixel size and the default 1.0 µm z-step, and flag both.

The analysis found 3 beads in the stack (21 planes of 64×64 pixels). Each one gives the same widths:

- **Lateral FWHM: 1.0 µm** (median, spread 0)
- **Axial FWHM: 2.0 µm** (median, spread 0)

These numbers depend on two values I had to assume, because the file doesn't record them:
- **Pixel size:** I used 1.0 µm, which is the 1x zoom setting the microscope is on now. If the stack was taken at 2x (0.5 µm pixels), the lateral width would be about 0.5 µm.
- **Z-step:** I used the default 1.0 µm. The axial width is 2 planes at that step, so a different z-step changes it directly.

With 1 µm pixels, a 1.0 µm lateral FWHM is only about one pixel, so the lateral figure is coarse and can't show a real difference between beads. If you tell me the zoom and z-step the stack was acquired with, I'll rerun it.
The box landed off-centre: the window reports its offset as (1048, -1048) µm. The frame is 2960 columns wide and 5056 rows high, so I used the wrong centre. Correcting it now.

The 400 × 300 pixel ROI box is now centred on the camera frame, at x 1280, y 2378 (top-left corner). The camera window reports zero offset from centre. The first attempt was off-centre and I corrected it. Only the display overlay changed; the stage and optics were not touched.

The camera ROI box moved 200 pixels to the right, from x=724 to x=924. It is still 600 × 300 pixels, and y is unchanged at 874. Its offset from the frame centre is now -256 µm horizontally and -1504 µm vertically.

The ROI box in the camera window is 600 µm wide and 300 µm high (600 × 300 pixels at 1.0 µm per pixel). Its top-left corner sits at x = 724, y = 874 in frame pixels, which is an offset of (−456, −1504) µm from the frame centre.

The ROI box is not centred. Its centre sits 400 µm off the frame centre, horizontally only. The box is 400 × 300 µm with its top-left corner at pixel (1680, 2378). Its centre is at (1880, 2528), and the frame centre is at (1480, 2528), so the box is 400 µm off along the window's x axis and vertically centred. The display reports the same offset (400 µm, 0 µm). I haven't changed anything. If you want it centred, I can move the box to the frame centre.

I haven't written the parameters yet. The config file already exists at `D:\claude-scratch\pr8\tmp\mesospim_eval_xhh_eezb\demo_config.py`, and saving over it would replace its current contents. Should I overwrite that file, or save to a different path so the existing one stays as it is?
The first picture came back as a blank 1×1 image, so I'll switch the main window to the Parameters tab and request the picture again.

The main window is now on the Parameters tab. I can't show you the picture, though: both capture attempts returned a 1×1 blank image, so the screenshot isn't usable. The tab switch itself was applied. If you want the page's values in text, I can read them from the instrument's state and config instead.
The camera view is back to the full image: the whole 2960 × 5056 px frame is shown, with the view set to fit. The instrument itself was not touched.

The camera window now shows only the upper-left quarter of the frame: the view is set to x 0, y 0, 1480 × 2528 pixels, out of the full 2960 × 5056 frame. This changed the display only; the instrument itself was not touched.
I'll check the configured image writers to find the OME-Zarr writer and its compression settings.
The OME-Zarr writer is set to zstd, so I'll change its compression to lz4 and leave the other settings alone.

The OME-Zarr writer now compresses with lz4 instead of zstd. I read the setting back and it shows lz4. The compression level is still 5, and the other writer settings are unchanged. This affects OME-Zarr writes from now on; the instrument is idle and nothing else was touched.
